acceptanceResults: An isolated micro-benchmark (not the full CLI, to remove unrelated startup/git/identity noise) quantifies the busy-poll overhead separately for a near-instant command and a multi-second command before changing any production code.

On cfg(unix), execute_captured waits for the child via a dedicated thread's blocking child.wait() plus a bounded mpsc recv_timeout on the main thread, instead of a sleep(10ms) polling loop; on timeout, the process is killed by pid and the final exit status is still collected, matching current timeout/kill/process-tree-cleanup semantics exactly.
cfg(windows) code path is textually unchanged.

New regression tests exercise a command that completes well under the poll interval, a command that runs past its deadline and must be killed (timed_out=true, passed=false), and confirm output capture and exit-code identity are unaffected.
cargo fmt, cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings, and cargo test --locked --workspace pass; no governance decision, evidence schema, or required-check semantics change.

Before/after measurement on this repository (WI-647 corrected harness or an equivalent isolated benchmark) shows a real, quantified reduction for short verification commands and no regression for long-running ones; no assumed speedup is claimed.
